newsitem.title: MEXICO: Thousands flock to image of Mexico's Subway Virgin.
newsitem.headline: Thousands flock to image of Mexico's Subway Virgin.

text.p: Nearly 2,000 people an hour are flocking to see an image of the so-called "Subway Virgin" formed in a puddle of water in a Mexico City Metro station, police said on Wednesday.

The image, now a stain left by the dried-up puddle, is about 10 inches (25 cm) long from head to toe, bearing a resemblance to the image of Mexico's Virgin of Guadalupe, a dark-skinned manifestation of the Virgin Mary.
"I believe, yes, that it is a miraculous appearance of the Virgin of Guadalupe," said Amanda Soliz, a supermarket worker.

The Mexican archbishop's office on Wednesday doubted the image was a true miracle, saying it failed to rank with divine appearances such as Guadalupe in 1531, Lourdes in France in 1854 and Fatima in Portugal in 1917.
"There are no theological elements that lead us to consider this a divine presence through these lines that have formed due to a water leak," the church office said in a statement.

The image first appeared on Sunday at the Hidalgo metro station in downtown Mexico City, home to one of the busiest underground railway systems in the world. The Mexico City Metro system transports more than a million people a day.
Police officers guarding the site said as many as 1,800 people per hour were lining up to see the image. Many people laid candles, flowers and coins near the site.
One police officer told reporters the monetary offerings totalled 1,300 pesos (about $165) on Tuesday, but he could not say where the money would end up.
